research.statement:
# CedarWorks Labs company knowledge
Fictional company knowledge base for ProofApply testing. Supplied knowledge, not a live web page. Illustrative site: https://cedarworks.example. The .example domain is not an actual employer website.
## Product context
CedarWorks Labs creates scheduling and booking software for small organizations. Its frontend team prioritizes clear forms, visible error states and interfaces that work with a keyboard.
## Engineering context
The frontend team values readable TypeScript, component tests and collaborative Git workflows. Docker appears as a preferred qualification in the fictional frontend opening. Some separate platform roles use Kubernetes. These company facts do not imply any candidate has those skills.
## Research question supported by this source
Which parts of a campus booking-interface project are relevant to the frontend opening? Form design, REST integration, error handling, tests, keyboard access and collaborative changes align with the product/team description.
No company headcount, salary, growth, customer counts or employment outcomes are supplied. Do not invent them.
research.uncertainty: Supplied knowledge; no live site verification.

claims.text: Campus Room Booker (January 2026 – April 2026): Built room-availability and booking-form screens using React and TypeScript. Integrated frontend with existing REST endpoints and implemented client-side form validation, loading indicators, and error handling for unsuccessful API responses.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Campus Room Booker — January 2026 to April 2026.
Mira built the room-availability view and booking-form screens using React and TypeScript.
She implemented client-side form validation, loading indicators and inline error messages.
Mira connected these screens to the team's existing REST endpoints for listing rooms and creating booking requests.
She handled unsuccessful API responses in the interface.

claims.text: Enhanced booking form accessibility by adding visible keyboard focus states, associated input labels, and accessible error text; manually verified keyboard flow. Authored 18 Vitest unit tests for validation and error states. Utilized Git branches and pull requests for collaborative development.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Mira added visible keyboard focus states, associated input labels and accessible inline error text to the booking form.
She manually checked the keyboard flow.
Mira authored 18 Vitest unit tests for the booking form's validation and error states.
Mira used Git branches and pull requests to submit her changes.

The course introduced cloud vocabulary, shared responsibility and basic service categories through lectures and quizzes.

verdicts.reason: The education details and expected graduation date are supported by the provided evidence. Frontend experience is supported by the project descriptions.
The listed skills are explicitly supported by the candidate's skills section in the resume.
The project details, including the timeline, technologies used, and specific frontend tasks, are supported by the project contribution report.
The accessibility work, unit testing, and Git workflow usage are all supported by the project contribution report.
The coursework completion date and content are supported by the provided course-completion evidence.

writing_notes: All statements are well-supported by the provided evidence.
The candidate correctly identifies the cloud foundations course as coursework rather than a professional certification.

uncertainty: Source support is not independent verification of self-reported experience.
Same-model semantic review may share writer errors.
